description: Returns the pages that already rank in classic search but under-earn — the worklist behind the Search Opportunities card (Visibility → Search). Two groups: "almostThere" (ranking 8–20, one improvement from page one) and "seenNotClicked" (already on page one, but a click rate well under THIS site's own page-one median — never an industry benchmark). Each page carries its searches, its totals, and whether it qualified on a single search or on the page's combined demand. Pair it with write-description / update-content to act on what it finds. Returns state "not_connected", "collecting" or "too_thin" when no honest verdict is possible.

source.description: Which engine to read: "google" or "bing". Omit for the richer one that has data.

name: agentimus-read-search-opportunities

impressions.description: The page's whole demand in the window.

missing.description: Pages ranking just off page one only: what is still left for the owner. "answer" — no paragraph answers the search; "title" — some searched words are not in the title searchers see; "link" — none of the site's own posts links here. Empty when nothing is (then `waiting` is true); null when the page could not be read, so nothing is claimed. Absent on the seen-not-clicked group.

postId.description: 0 when the URL maps to no post.

searches.description: How many distinct searches found this page.

waiting.description: True when the owner's side is done and only the engine's next report can move this page — no edit is left to ask for.

wholePage.description: True when the PAGE's combined demand qualified rather than any single search — the shape an engine produces when one page's traffic arrives as many long-tail searches.

collisions.description: Searches that several pages are splitting: the engine sends one search to one page at a time, so competing pages take turns and every turn a weaker page takes is a click the strong one loses. The heaviest few, ranked by showings.

best.description: Best average position among the competing pages.

clicks.description: Clicks the pages earned between them.

archive.description: True when this page is a tag, category or other term archive — a list of posts, not an answer. When an archive splits a search with a post, the post is the answer whatever `winner` says: advise the owner to set the archive aside on the Search screen (set-aside-page takes post IDs, so an agent cannot), and never advise editing the post to point at the archive.

postId.description: 0 when the URL never resolved to a post.

share.description: This page's fraction of the query's showings (0–1).

winner.description: True on the one page that earns the click — most clicks, then the better position. Advise keeping this page as the answer and pointing the others at it, or differentiating them; never advise editing the winner.

query.description: The search several pages are splitting, as the engine reported it.

shown.description: Times the search showed any of these pages, summed.

worst.description: Worst average position among the competing pages.

collisionsTotal.description: How many split searches exist in total; the list above carries the heaviest few.

opportunities.description: Pages worth looking at, both groups.

setAside.description: Pages the owner excused from this worklist.

ctrBar.description: The click-rate threshold actually applied to "seenNotClicked" (percentage): a page must fall BELOW this, not merely below medianCtr. Quote this, never medianCtr, when stating what "not clicked enough" means.

medianCtr.description: This site's own page-one median click rate (percentage) — the bar "seenNotClicked" is measured against. Null when no honest bar can be set, in which case that group stays empty and medianReason says why.

medianNeeds.description: How many it takes before a bar is computed at all.

medianReason.description: Why there is no bar, when medianCtr is null: "thin" = too few page-one results carry enough views to measure (says nothing about clicking); "unclicked" = enough exist and the middle one earned no clicks at all. Empty string when a bar exists. Never report one of these as the other.

medianRows.description: How many page-one results carried enough views to measure a click rate.

dismissed.description: ⭐ THE OWNER’S OWN LEDGER, WHOLE — not the capped `examples` list above. These are decisions, not rules: each one can be put back with dismiss-search, and this is the only way to find out what is in it. ⛔ Read this before concluding a search "isn’t reported" — it may simply have been set aside.

impressions.description: Views it drew across this site’s pages in the window, 0 when no engine reports it any more.

query.description: A search the owner set aside, in the one spelling the ledger stores.

kind.description: WHY this one was left out — ⛔ they are not the same claim. "operator" = it uses site:/inurl:/intitle: and the like, which is how machines search rather than people. "address" = a web address somebody put in the search box. "paste" = far longer than anything a person types, usually a prompt or a paragraph. "dismissed" = the OWNER set this search aside (put it back with dismiss-search). ⛔ Only "operator" is evidence about WHO searched; a pasted address says nothing about the searcher.

probeShare.description: Percentage of the reported views that were search-operator probes — the ONLY number here that supports saying "these were not people". Always less than or equal to `share`, which also counts searches left out for reasons that say nothing about who typed them.

searches.description: Distinct searches left out of every judgement here (one search on six pages counts once). ⛔ For FOUR different reasons — read `examples[].kind` before describing them as anything.

share.description: Percentage of the reported views left out of the judgements here, for ANY of the four reasons. These are excluded from every judgement (no title rewrite makes a scraper click, and no edit answers a URL), which is why read-search-performance — the raw record — reports larger numbers. A high share is the real story on a site with no worklist: state it before concluding anything about how the pages are performing. ⛔ Do NOT describe this share as machine traffic — that claim belongs to `probeShare` alone.

outOfScope.description: How many measured PAGES this report deliberately says nothing about, because the owner switched their content type off for checking. Above zero means these lists cover part of the measured site, not all of it — the pages are not missing, they are excluded on purpose. Pages with no post behind them (the home page, archives) are never excluded, since no content type governs them.

impressions.description: The page's whole demand in the window.

missing.description: Pages ranking just off page one only: what is still left for the owner. "answer" — no paragraph answers the search; "title" — some searched words are not in the title searchers see; "link" — none of the site's own posts links here. Empty when nothing is (then `waiting` is true); null when the page could not be read, so nothing is claimed. Absent on the seen-not-clicked group.

postId.description: 0 when the URL maps to no post.

searches.description: How many distinct searches found this page.

waiting.description: True when the owner's side is done and only the engine's next report can move this page — no edit is left to ask for.

wholePage.description: True when the PAGE's combined demand qualified rather than any single search — the shape an engine produces when one page's traffic arrives as many long-tail searches.

source.description: The engine these numbers came from; empty when none has data yet.

dropped.description: Rows the last poll could not store, because the snapshot keeps only its busiest N. What is missing is the quiet tail — say so rather than treating the stored set as everything.

pageCap.description: Always 0 now: Bing is worked through a few pages per poll until every page has been asked about, so no page sits permanently outside anything.

dropped.description: Rows the last poll could not store, because the snapshot keeps only its busiest N. The engines report clicks-descending, so what is missing is the quiet tail — say so rather than treating the stored set as everything.

pageCap.description: Always 0: no source samples a fixed set of pages any more. Kept so readers that branch on it keep taking their no-sampling path.
